Zhang, J., Meerman, H., Benders, R. and Faaij, A. (2020). Comprehensive review of current natural gas liquefaction processes on technical and economic performance. Applied Thermal Engineering 166, 114736. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2019.114736

Locators are printed journal page numbers (= PDF pages). Main file: Table 15 harmonized ranges for seven liquefaction processes, each split into technical-report and academic-literature processes; capacity (MTPA) and either gas-turbine fuel (the printed primary energy input, GJ HHV/GJ HHV LNG, = specific work / assumed GT efficiency) or, for DMR (electric-motor drive assumed), electricity derived as specific work/0.95/3.6. Specific work (kJ/kg LNG) also loaded as target not-stated in kWh/t (= kJ/kg / 3.6) and kept in _other-values. Capex ranges (Sect. 4.2.1) and production cost (4.2.2) attached to two plant-level technologies; per-process capex and cost breakdown are only in Figs 8-9 (charts, not extracted). All costs 2018 Q2 USD (IHS UCCI). Table 15 cells wrap across lines in the PDF; values were reassembled (e.g. 1166.4-138/2.4 = 1382.4) and should be spot-checked. No numeric data in Tables 1-14 (qualitative).

Abstract gives specific capex 124-2255 $/TPA; Sect. 4.2.1 gives academic 125-1285 and technical reports 220-2255. Driver efficiencies are the authors assumptions, so fuel rows are model-derived, not measured.
